_doc: How the four elements look (design 8; elemental_system_journal.md M8).
Presentation only. The elements themselves are code and their gameplay
numbers live in elements.json -- this file is the other half of the same
split weapons.json and weapon_visuals.json already use, so nothing here
is ever read by the resolver.
Each element names a colour, a marker shape, an optional authored rig
for its aura and its status, and a particle preset. A rig is optional on
purpose: only Thunder has an authored aura today and only Fire an
authored status flame, so everything else falls back to the procedural
ring, which is the design's own baseline (8, considerations).
`marker` is a shape, not a colour: an element has to be readable without
relying on hue (design 8, colourblind proposal).
The procedural ring and marker, kept as the fallback for an element
with no rig and for the locked slot, which has no sprite at all.
`rig_scale` is the one field the authored path uses: an aura sprite is
drawn `rig_scale` times the body's diameter, keeping the art's own
aspect rather than being squeezed into a square. Above 1 because these
effects are rings *around* a body and have to clear it.
Elemental particles are capped per frame, separately from the pool's
own MAX_PARTICLES, so a hundred auras can never starve the hit
bursts and the death poofs of theirs (design 9, particle budget).
Authored art for a status, keyed by the status id the combat layer
uses -- not by element. Fire's burn and Ice's freeze are the two
that have art; `chill` has none and falls back to its procedural
chevron, which is why this is a map with gaps rather than a field
on each element.
`burn` is shared with the weapon blessings' own burn: the elemental
one is the same status with a `bound_to_aura` flag, so it has to
look the same.
One entry per reaction (combat/elements/config.py REACTION_PAIRS).
`rig` is the authored burst; where one is named the procedural
Flash does not draw at all (M10 rule 2). `seconds` is how long it
stays on screen -- these draw over every character, so the number
is deliberately small and deliberately here, where it is easy to
change, rather than buried as a constant in transient.py.
`size` is the sprite's drawn width in world pixels at the smallest
a reaction ever is; the resolver hands the flash a radius from the
reaction's own reach, and the drawn size scales with it, so a
wide-reaching Overload looks wider than a Frostburn on one body.
`label` is optional and names which of the two elements is the
*fill* of the popped reaction name and which is the *ring* round it
(M11 C). Left out, they follow REACTION_PAIRS order. It exists
because that order is taxonomy -- it also decides the blend and the
art -- and which colour reads better on the inside of a word is a
separate question with a separate answer.
